subject: Discovery recap & quick check on priority
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <ep@bridgewell.health>, Mark Sullivan <msullivan@bridgewell.health>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap & proposed next steps

Hi Elena / Mark —

Thanks again for the quick discovery earlier today. High-level recap and proposed next steps so we can align: 

Call highlights:
- Primary goal: reduce inference latency variability for clinical triage models during peak hours (current 95th pctl spikes to ~1.2s).
- Constraint: PHI-sensitive data; BridgeWell needs SOC2 evidence and an option for private network deployments (VPC/on-prem patterns).
- Ops: Traffic is bursty (daily morning/evening spikes) and batch windows exist for non-real-time workloads.

What I think makes sense next: 
1) 2-week pilot benchmark (Redwood Dedicated) — we run a representative workload with your models and traffic patterns, measure latency, throughput, and cost per token.
2) Security pack & artifacts — share SOC2 report, network architecture notes, and our data handling addendum.
3) Mutual action plan doc to lock timelines and owners.

I've attached our discovery notes and a simple MAP spreadsheet that maps owners and milestones. Proposed timing: start pilot week of June 14 if that still works for you.

Next steps I need from you:
- Confirm whether the pilot start window (week of Jun 14) works.
- Share a non-prod dataset pointer or the representative inference traces (S3 link) and an internal point-of-contact for dataset access.

If you'd prefer a different pilot shape (shorter smoke test + deeper benchmark), happy to adapt.

Thanks — looking forward to your thoughts.

Rafael Mendes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rafael@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: discovery-notes-bridgewell-20260601.pdf (notes), bridgewell-map-maP-v1.xlsx (owners/milestones)

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <ep@bridgewell.health>, Mark Sullivan <msullivan@bridgewell.health>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap & proposed next steps — pilot options and a small incentive

Hi Elena / Mark —

Wanted to follow up with a slightly different approach in case timing or capacity is the blocker. Two options that have worked well with other health-tech customers: 

Option A — Fast smoke + report (5 business days)
- Lightweight test using a 2k/hr synthetic trace representative of your peak shape.
- Deliverables: latency distribution, cost estimate, short ops notes.
- No network change required (we can run against sample inputs / synthetic traces).

Option B — Full 2-week benchmark (proposed earlier)
- Run at scale on a Dedicated pool with your model, measure sustained p99/p95, throughput, and cost per request.
- Includes pilot credits and a short ops review call.

Pilot incentive: if you kick off a paid benchmark before June 30 we can provide a 30% pilot credit (applies to the benchmark run).

If the project is not a current priority, a one-line reply works too — e.g., “paused” or “not a fit” — that helps us prioritize outreach for other partners.

Link to the MAP and a short checklist: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3c-MAP-Bridgewell
HubSpot record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/company/bridgewell-health

Would you be open to either a quick 20-min sync next week to pick A/B and confirm dataset access? If not, I can follow up again in a few weeks.

Thanks,
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rafael@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

P.S. Camila (cc) — our Solutions Engineer — can run the smoke test and coordinate S3 access once we have the pointer.

Attachments: discovery-notes-bridgewell-20260601.pdf
